item: A long gate hold in the storage-events journal carries what its holder thread was doing in the kernel (ws, gap, rq), counted once a second from /proc, paid for by writing frames at their measured width
refs: coordinator 17 Oct; OSM gate census REPORT section 2; PR #1429
summary: The 16 Oct holds of 30 to 182 s could not be told apart as slow work or a stalled thread. holder_state looks at the holder once a second while a hold is past 30 s and already journaled (3 small /proc reads, 29 microseconds, on the watchdog thread) and counts six classes: run, futex, nap (SQLite's busy handler), disk, other (a wait the kernel named otherwise), unknown (a sleep it printed nothing for); gap is the longest time between two looks; rq is the seconds the holder waited for a CPU from the first look to the last, the exact difference of schedstat's second total to 0.1 s, null (never 0) when fewer than two looks could read it. Counting R looks as running or runnable was dropped: measured with the real look on two cores, a holder on a CPU 48 per cent of the time read R in 17 per cent of its looks and one that waited for a CPU 12 per cent of the time read it in 33 per cent, and 22 to 34 per cent of looks in three of five scenarios were a sleep with no wchan (the OSM gate lab's finding, reproduced). The first look counts nothing (it is where rq starts); the thread's name and the kernel symbol are never kept; off Linux the hold says ws null with ws_why unsupported-os; counts reach the journal at the 15 s tick and at the release, not once a second. futex is a floor for GIL waits (a look hands the GIL to its only waiter). Bytes: 57 per hold at the widest for ws and gap (+14 for the ws_why null a cleared reason leaves, +13 for rq), and 827 in the method (+242 for rq and the class change), paid by writer.FRAME_CHARS = 79, the measured maximum of module:function:line under src/, pinned both ways against every function by an AST walk (it was 90 in the first cut, 11 characters nothing had measured), which frees 4,740 bytes the model counted for frames no real event has; the widest journal is 124,251 bytes with all 20 splits (749 free; the widest hold event is 1,222 bytes; both pinned by tests/test_storage_events.py like FRAME_CHARS), the fixed part 5,176 to 6,003 before rq and 6,245 with it. Also fixes a flake: the phase tests counted samples of the module's gate while the process's own watchdog thread could tick in the same hold (about 8 per cent of runs).
